methods.description: Split a composite polygon into two or more non-overlapping rectangles; derive missing lengths by addition/subtraction where needed, calculate each rectangle area and add.
Split into a rectangle and a triangle, identify or derive the perpendicular triangle height, multiply base by height then halve and add to the rectangle area.
Calculate the complete enclosing rectangle/square area, calculate the removed rectangular or triangular areas, including repeated equal pieces, and subtract their total once.

Add the areas of overlapping rectangles, then subtract the rectangular shared patch once because adding the two areas counts that patch twice; elementary add/subtract counting adaptation, no filled original overlap example claimed.
Convert mixed centimetre/metre lengths to one length unit before decomposing; use whole/benchmark decimal mental facts or repeated addition for the simple areas, then add square units.

theory.intro: A **composite figure** is made from simpler shapes joined together. Find its area by splitting it into rectangles and triangles and adding, or by subtracting a missing piece from a large rectangle.
facts: Area of a rectangle $=$ length $\times$ width.
Find any missing side length from the other lengths, since opposite sides of the whole figure add up.
Area of a triangle $=$ base $\times$ perpendicular height $\div2$.
Use the same length unit and write areas in squared units.
When rectangles overlap, count the shared area only once.
steps: Split the figure into simple shapes, or show the whole shape and the piece to remove.
Work out any missing lengths and use the same length unit.
Calculate the area of each simple shape.
Add or subtract the areas as needed and write squared units.

workedExamples.solution_text:
The upper rectangle has height $11-4=7\text{ cm}$.
Split along the dashed line.
$A=13\times4+5\times7$
$=52+35$
$=87\text{ cm}^2$
Alternatively, split vertically. The lower-right rectangle has width $13-5=8\text{ cm}$.
$A=5\times11+8\times4$
$=55+32$
$=87\text{ cm}^2$
Both ways count the whole shape once.

Triangle height: $10-4=6\text{ m}$.
Rectangle area
$A_1=9\times4$
$=36\text{ m}^2$
Triangle area
$A_2=9\times6\div2$
$=54\div2$
$=27\text{ m}^2$
$A=A_1+A_2$
$=36+27$
$=63\text{ m}^2$

(a) Subtract the window area from the whole wall area.
$A=12\times7-3\times2$
$=84-6$
$=78\text{ m}^2$
(b) The missing triangle is half of the $5\text{ cm}$ by $4\text{ cm}$ corner rectangle.
$A=11\times7-5\times4\div2$
$=77-10$
$=67\text{ cm}^2$

Adding both mat areas counts the shared rectangle twice. Subtract its area once.
$A=8\times5+7\times4-2\times3$
$=40+28-6$
$=68-6$
$=62\text{ m}^2$

workedExamples.question_text: An L-shaped room is $300\text{ cm}$ high and $150\text{ cm}$ wide at the upper section. The lower section extends $7\text{ m}$ beyond it and is $2\text{ m}$ high. Find the floor area in $\text{m}^2$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Use metres for all lengths.
$300\text{ cm}=3\text{ m}$ and $150\text{ cm}=1.5\text{ m}$.
The first rectangle covers the full height.
$A_1=1.5\times3$
$=4.5\text{ m}^2$
The lower extension is a separate rectangle.
$A_2=7\times2$
$=14\text{ m}^2$
$A=A_1+A_2$
$=4.5+14$
$=18.5\text{ m}^2$
